solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Eccentric bishop with a lot of sumptuous material

parts.note: an eccentric is a cam, an off-centre wheel in machinery
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most of it, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: sumptuous means rich

explanation.surface: An odd churchman decked out in plenty of luxurious fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like an anagram signal but is the noun CAM; 'a lot of' cuts RICH to RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine linen or cotton fabric, a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Catalogue famous poem penned by Buffalo Bill

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the poem sits inside the name

parts.note: Buffalo Bill was William Cody, the Wild West showman
If is Kipling's famous poem

explanation.surface: A list of well-known verse written by the Wild West showman.
explanation.definitionFit: To codify is to arrange laws or rules into a systematic collection, as to catalogue is.

clue.text: Becoming gentler — but cutting about European Liberals!

indicators.note: about means around, so the cutting surrounds the letters

parts.note: mowing is cutting grass
L is Liberal, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Softening, yet slashing at Europe's liberal politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Mellowing is softening with age or experience, growing less harsh.

clue.text: Take back tons wagoner brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means raised from bottom to top, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: a carter drives a wagon, as a wagoner does

explanation.surface: Return a heavy load that a cart driver delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to withdraw a statement, to take it back.

clue.text: Beast of burden, one oddly biting head of harmless reptile

indicators.note: biting means having in its teeth, so the beast holds the letter

parts.note: a camel is a beast of burden

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of the next word
oddly means in a strange arrangement, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A pack animal, oddly, bites the head of an inoffensive lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like a call for odd letters, but here it rearranges ONE into EON.
explanation.definitionFit: The chameleon is a colour-changing lizard, which is a reptile.

clue.text: Teacher dons formal wear to work for press

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the teacher is wrapped in the clothing

parts.note: a suit is formal wear
BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teacher's degree, standing for a teacher

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher puts on a smart outfit to go to work for the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: BEd (Bachelor of Education) stands for a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: To subedit is to correct and prepare copy for printing, editing work done for the press.

clue.text: It may finally be raised, say — in seconds, that is

indicators.note: in puts the example word inside the abbreviation for that is

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is
eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: Something may be lifted at last, in a matter of seconds, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: A siege is raised when the attackers withdraw or the town is relieved.
explanation.definitionFit: A siege is a blockade of a town, and ends when it is lifted.

clue.text: Dog swallowing English wife's charm

indicators.note: swallowing means taking inside, so the dog holds the letters

parts.note: a bitch is a female dog
W is the abbreviation for wife, with the apostrophe s read as is

explanation.surface: A hound gobbles up an English wife's lucky trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewitch is to cast a spell over, to enchant or charm.

clue.text: Engraver's daughter on river Ribble to begin with

definitions.note: the apostrophe s reads as is, the definition being the engraver

parts.note: the Ure is a Yorkshire river

indicators.note: to begin with picks out the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An engraver's daughter is beside the Ribble, a Lancashire river, at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire; the Ribble supplies only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was the great German Renaissance engraver and painter.

clue.text: Added up books sent up by lanky journalist

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up means raised from bottom to top, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books
lanky means tall
ED, editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: Counted books mocked by a gangly reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Totalled means summed, the figures counted to a final amount.

clue.text: Alert few excited by duke's pottery

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A few watchful people are thrilled by a nobleman's ceramics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges ALERT FEW into ELFTWARE, placed after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Delftware is the blue-and-white tin-glazed earthenware made at Delft, a type of ceramic ware.

clue.text: Best way to follow revolutionary argument

indicators.note: to follow places the way after the reversed argument
revolutionary means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a row is an argument
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: The best route comes after a heated political quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns ROW into WOR; 'Best' is a verb meaning defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To worst someone is to defeat them, as to best them is.

clue.text: Admitted by Italian monk, look at plants

indicators.note: admitted by means let inside, so the word goes into the monk

parts.note: Fra is the title of an Italian friar
lo is an old word for look!

explanation.surface: An Italian friar lets someone in to view the vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is the plant life of a region, as fauna is its animals.

clue.text: English reader with a list primarily of voters

parts.note: a lector is a reader, as in church or a university

indicators.note: primarily picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An English reader with a list mainly of people who vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Electoral is the adjective relating to electors, those who vote.

clue.text: Where the setter may be, if the cluing is substandard!

definitions.text: Where the setter may be, if the cluing is substandard!

parts.words: Where the setter may be, if the cluing is substandard!
parts.note: a compiler who writes poor clues would be in disgrace with solvers, and a setter is also a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A setter who writes bad clues would be out of favour.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is on setter: a crossword compiler and a gun dog, who would both end up in a kennel of sorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the doghouse is an idiom for being in disgrace with someone.

clue.text: Bewilder old boy, and reportedly worry girl

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: worry is fuss and Kate is a girl's name, said together

explanation.surface: Confuse a former pupil and, they say, trouble a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To obfuscate is to make obscure or confusing, so to perplex.

clue.text: Nerve trapped by a French worker lacking in courtesy

indicators.note: trapped by means held inside, so the nerve goes between the other pieces

parts.note: un is French for a
an ant is a worker
gall is nerve, cheek

explanation.surface: Cheek caught by a French labourer who has no manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungallant describes a man not chivalrous or polite to women, discourteous.

clue.text: Eg Oxford man, one catching fish in African swamp

definitions.text: one catching fish in African swamp

parts.note: an Oxford is a type of laced shoe
Bill is a man's name

explanation.surface: An Oxford man is fishing in an African marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford man' suggests a university graduate, but Oxford is a shoe and the man is Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoebill is a large stork-like bird of East African swamps that eats fish.

clue.text: Dance featuring light female in tall heather?

indicators.note: in puts the light female inside the tall heather

parts.note: tall means high
ling is a name for heather
to light is to land, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: A dance in which a dainty woman frolics among tall heather, presumably in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' is the verb, to alight, so LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highland fling is a lively Scottish solo dance.

clue.text: Expression of amusement over fat religious reformer

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: LOL, laugh out loud, expresses amusement
lard is fat

explanation.surface: Laughing at a stout churchman bent on change.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lollard was a follower of John Wycliffe, an early English church reformer.

clue.text: Discernment one Saint displayed in hours of darkness

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: displayed in means shown inside, so the saint's letter goes within the darkness

parts.note: night is the hours of darkness

explanation.surface: A holy person shows wisdom during the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is deep understanding, the power to perceive clearly.

clue.text: She was a goddess at that time in A&E

definitions.note: the phrase names a female deity, standing as a noun

indicators.note: in puts the time word inside the hospital department

parts.note: A and E, accident and emergency, written as its two letters
then means at that time

explanation.surface: A woman once divine, at that moment in hospital casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene, or Athena, was the Greek deity of wisdom.

clue.text: Open sleeve mostly recycled for wrappers

indicators.note: recycled means made into something new, so the letters are reworked
mostly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

explanation.surface: An open sleeve, nearly all of it, turned into packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SLEEVE to SLEEV; 'recycled' rearranges OPEN SLEEV.
explanation.definitionFit: Envelopes are paper covers for letters, a kind of wrapping.

clue.text: Some love dictating early Sanskrit

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A little affection while dictating ancient Indian texts.
explanation.definitionFit: Vedic is the oldest form of Sanskrit, the language of the Vedas.

clue.text: Hoofed mammal nibbling oriental plant

indicators.note: nibbling means holding in its mouth, so the animal contains the letter

parts.note: a pony is a hoofed mammal
E, for east, means oriental

explanation.surface: A pony munching an Eastern flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The peony is a garden flower with large showy blooms.

clue.text: Hints about touring large Adriatic port

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the reversed hints surround the letter
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tips are hints

explanation.surface: Travel tips for a big tour of an Adriatic harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TIPS into SPIT, and 'touring' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is a port city on the Dalmatian coast of Croatia.

clue.text: State support part of UK rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: aid is support
NI, Northern Ireland, is part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A government refuses to back a region of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a sovereign nation, a country being a state.

clue.text: Drink advert: Oscar phoned Derek regularly about that

parts.note: Oscar is the radio alphabet word for O
rang means phoned

indicators.note: about means around, so the pair of letters goes round the advert
regularly takes every other letter of the name

parts.note: an ad is an advert

explanation.surface: A man called Oscar rang Derek to discuss a soft drink commercial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of Derek; 'about' puts them either side of the advert. 'Drink advert' reads as one phrase but splits at 'Drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a fizzy soft drink flavoured with oranges.

clue.text: Clearly this writer had pounds invested in girl

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the letters go into the girl's name

parts.note: Lucy is a girl's name
the setter would say I'd for I had
L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin librae

explanation.surface: Plainly, the writer had money tied up in a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucidly means in a clear, easily understood way.

clue.text: Qualify in French, given book

parts.note: en is French for in
a title is a book, as in a publisher's list of titles

explanation.surface: Pass a French exam, rewarded with a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone is to give them a right, to make them eligible.
